title: 5 signs it's perimenopause, not stress
description: The five symptoms Indian women most often mistake for 'just stress' or 'just getting older' — and the hormonal reason behind each one.

slides.headline: Mood swings that feel out of character
slides.body: Oestrogen helps regulate serotonin, the brain chemical that stabilises mood. As it fluctuates, sudden irritability or tearfulness can appear with no obvious trigger — it's hormonal, not a personality change.

slides.headline: You wake up at 3am for no reason
slides.body: Falling asleep is fine. Staying asleep is the problem. Falling progesterone, an earlier cortisol rise, and shifting body temperature all converge in the early hours — it's one of the most common and most precise symptoms women report.

slides.headline: Brain fog at the worst possible moments
slides.body: Forgetting words mid-sentence or losing your train of thought in a meeting isn't a sign something is wrong with you. Hormonal shifts affect memory and focus directly — and it usually improves once levels settle.

slides.headline: Weight that won't move, no matter what you try
slides.body: Declining oestrogen changes where your body stores fat, often shifting it to the abdomen. Diet and exercise still matter, but they're not the whole story — hormones are too.

slides.headline: Periods that stop following the rules
slides.body: Lighter, heavier, shorter, skipped entirely — changing cycles are often the very first sign of perimenopause, sometimes years before any other symptom shows up.
